item.title: Shirahama: White Sand Beach and Ancient Hot Springs — Guide
item.description: Shirahama, on Wakayama’s southwestern coast, is one of Japan’s oldest and most popular hot-spring resorts, its name literally meaning ‘white beach’. Shirarahama Beach curves for 600 metres in dazzling white sand — famously replenished with sand from Australia — while the town’s onsen are among the three oldest in Japan, recorded in 7th-century chronicles as a retreat for emperors. Beyond the beach lie dramatic coastal sights: the sheer cliffs of Sandanbeki, the sunset-framed sea arch of Engetsuto island, and Saki-no-yu, a rustic open-air bath set on the rocks where waves break metres away.
